agent_notes: In the Hebrew numbering the superscription 'mizmor' is part of verse 1 (KJV 98:0 and 98:1 are merged here), so the verse carries the heading as its first word.

הוֹשִׁיעָה is a feminine perfect with a feminine subject 'right hand' (yamin, fem.) and 'arm' (zeroa', fem.) following; the verb agrees with the nearer/first subject and the second is added. The literal layer renders it as singular 'has saved' with both subjects after it. KJV 'gotten him the victory' and BBE 'overcome' are looser than 'saved for him'; ASV and YLT are closest.
STEPBible glosses 'it has given victory'; I kept the root yasha' as 'saved' in the literal layer so the tie to yeshu'ah (v.2) and yeshu'at (v.3) stays visible.

agent_notes: Revised after the review: Radak on Psalm 98:2 is cited for the near-synonym reading (the last half-verse explains the first); Malbim is cited separately for his distinction, in which righteousness is the attribute that moves God to act and salvation is the act it produces. The commentary now presents the two as different views.

הוֹדִיעַ and גִּלָּה are Hebrew perfects, and Ibn Ezra glosses הודיע as 'past tense'. I translated them as present-perfect ('has made known', 'has uncovered'), as STEPBible and all five English versions do.

agent_notes: Yir'am is from ra'am 'to thunder', used of the sea in Ps 96:11 as 'roar' (yir'am). KJV 'roar' is acceptable but loses that the verb is the verb for thunder; the ancient audience hears the sea as storm-thunder. Chosen: 'thunder' in the literal layer.

agent_notes: Revised after the review: בָא is morphologically ambiguous between perfect ('has come': STEPBible's tagging, YLT, BBE) and participle ('is coming': KJV, ASV). The translation chooses the participle, because the verse sets it against the future יִשְׁפֹּט, and says so. The Targum's אֲתָא looks like a perfect, which supports the other reading, so this is a judgment call.
